territorial_scope.description: Applies to testing of autonomous motor vehicles on public roadways in Washington State.

evidence.quote: for the purposes of testing in Washington state

summary.short: Amends Washington rules for the department's autonomous vehicle self-certification testing pilot (RCW 46.92.010). Testing entities must provide information, report collisions and moving violations, and give advance notice to law enforcement. Also amends RCW 46.37.480 on headsets while driving. Section 1 takes effect October 1, 2022.
summary.long: Amends RCW 46.92.010 for the department's autonomous vehicle self-certification testing pilot program. Before testing on public roadways, a self-certifying entity must provide contact information, planned local jurisdictions, vehicle identification numbers where required, and proof of insurance under RCW 46.30.050. Vehicles without a required identification number must be assigned and display a unique number. The entity must notify the department of reportable collisions and of moving violations involving the vehicle during testing, state whether the autonomous driving system was operating, and submit an annual report by February 1. It must give written notice to local and state law enforcement 14 to 60 days before testing. The department may adopt a fee to offset program administration, must make submitted information publicly accessible, and must report annually to the house and senate transportation committees. Autonomous vehicles may not be operated for testing until the information is provided. Autonomous is defined as SAE J3016 level four or five. Section 2 amends RCW 46.37.480, which bars operating a motor vehicle while wearing headsets or earphones that exclude other sounds, subject to listed exceptions. Section 1 takes effect October 1, 2022, and the Section 2 effective date is set in Section 4. The text states no penalty amounts.
